issues.title: Undefined continuation update at the allowed cardinality boundary
issues.failure_explanation: Let S denote the set written as \(\mathcal{K}+1\). Choose a full-spark matrix A, an index set I of size m, a vector z with all magnitudes greater than \(\mu_k\), and \(b=A_Iz\). Then the feasible vector supported on I with values z, together with its threshold vector, is an admissible BCD fixed point satisfying \(\mathcal Q_{\mu_k}=m<\operatorname{spark}(A)=m+1\). Since \(c_{k+1}=\mu_k/\rho<\mu_k\), S is the zero complement of I, so \(|S|=n-m\) and the old radical contains 0 divided by \(m-n+|S|=0\). Thus the real-valued update is undefined. Independently, substituting the threshold operator into the surrogate gives \(\mathcal Q_c=\sum_{i\in S}x_i^2/c^2+n-|S|\); using the full m+1 budget yields the denominator \(m-n+|S|+1\), as used in version 2.
issues.overall_effect: The outer continuation procedure can fail to produce a next threshold on a valid state with exactly m entries above the trial threshold, so its claimed preservation of invertibility and numerical stability is not assured. The fixed-parameter BCD updates and their formal convergence results do not depend on this continuation rule.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the continuation bound from Q_c(x,H_c(x)) = c^{-2} sum_{i in S} x_i^2 + n-|S| using the available spark budget m+1, and replace the denominator in (updatemu) by m-n+|S|+1. This makes the radical defined at |S|=n-m, including the exhibited zero-complement fixed point, while leaving the continuation procedure and all fixed-parameter BCD results otherwise unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old denominator is coherent away from the boundary as a stricter bound, so the added +1 is not a uniquely forced transcriptional correction without checking the surrogate and cardinality calculation; the defect is therefore more than a typo. That check and repair are nevertheless short, routine, and confined to one continuation update, preserve the intended invertibility guarantee, and require no new lemma, proof architecture, model restriction, or loss in any affected result.
